title: The hooked galaxy and its companion
caption: The hooked galaxy and its companion in Libra, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: MCG-01-39-003, NGC 5917 · constellation Libra · about 90 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This color image, titled the hooked galaxy and its companion, shows the galaxy pair cataloged as MCG-01-39-003 and NGC 5917. According to the image metadata, the pair lies about 90 million light-years away in the constellation Libra. A galaxy pair is two galaxies close enough on the sky, and often in space, to be studied together.

The data were gathered with the FORS1 multi-mode instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope for the European Supernova Collaboration in April and May 2006. Observations through four filters, B, V, R and I, were combined to make the color picture.

The field of view measures 5.6 x 8.3 arcminutes, with north at the top and east to the left. Ferdinando Patat and the Paranal Science team carried out the observations, and Olivia Blanchemain, Henri Boffin and Haennes Heyer of ESO handled the final processing. The European Supernova Collaboration studies supernovae, the explosions that end the lives of some stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.50 x 6.63 arcminutes) and distance (90 million light years), the frame spans roughly 118,000 × 174,000 light-years. Its light set out about 90 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 on the Very Large Telescope observed the field through B, V, R and I filters, from 440 to 768 nm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.

understand.eye: Part of the light is near-infrared, invisible to the eye, and the telescope's exposures gather far more light than an eye can.
